methods.label: Compare decimal digits
methods.explanation:
A bar means that the marked digits repeat forever. Append zeros to the terminating decimal so that the choices can be compared place by place:
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=9.12344000\ldots,\\
B&=9.12344444\ldots,\\
C&=9.12343434\ldots,\\
D&=9.12342342\ldots,\\
E&=9.12341234\ldots.
\end{aligned}
\]
All five agree through the first four decimal places. At the fifth decimal place, \(A\) and \(B\) have \(4\), while \(C,D,E\) have \(3,2,1\), respectively. Thus the largest must be \(A\) or \(B\). At the sixth decimal place, \(B\) has \(4\) and \(A\) has \(0\). Therefore the largest number is \(9.123\overline4\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Expanding the marked repeating blocks and comparing decimal places requires only elementary place value.
